questions.q: Why does this lesson argue "open-weight" is a more accurate term than "open-source" for a model like Llama 4?
options: Because Llama 4 is actually a closed model
Because you typically get the trained weights and a license, not the training data or training code — unlike traditional open-source software
Because "open-weight" is simply a shorter phrase
Because Llama 4 has no license at all
questions.explain: Open-source software traditionally includes source code and the ability to rebuild from scratch; open-weight models distribute only the trained weights under a license, which is a narrower form of openness.

questions.q: Which license did this lesson verify for DeepSeek V4?
options: A fully proprietary, closed license
MIT license
No license at all
A government-restricted license
questions.explain: DeepSeek V4's Flash and Pro checkpoints are MIT-licensed, one of the more permissive open-weight licenses available.

questions.q: What is a genuine advantage of a closed, hosted-API model over an open-weight model?
options: It's always free to use
It's a fully managed, scaling, continuously updated service with no infrastructure to run yourself
It always comes with the full training dataset
It never has any usage policy restrictions
questions.explain: Closed models trade away weight access and policy flexibility for a fully managed service — no GPUs, scaling, or deployment to maintain yourself.

questions.q: What is a genuine advantage of an open-weight model over a closed one?
options: It requires no operational effort at all
You can self-host, fine-tune without external approval, and audit exactly what's running
It is always more capable than any closed model
It never needs updating
questions.explain: Open-weight models let you control hosting, fine-tuning, and auditing directly — at the cost of owning the operational burden of running them yourself.

questions.q: According to the lesson, how do most real organizations actually approach open vs. closed models?
options: They exclusively use open-weight models and never touch closed APIs
They exclusively use closed APIs and never self-host anything
They often use both — a closed flagship for the hardest tasks, open-weight for high-volume or sensitive workloads
They are legally required to pick only one
questions.explain: Most teams mix both approaches, matching each to the task: a closed flagship for the hardest reasoning work, and self-hosted open-weight models for cost-sensitive or data-sensitive workloads.
